text:
anya: heads-up — we've been seeing a spike in 429s for eu-west dedicated pools over the last 20m. noticed a pattern where short bursts cause large tails in queueing and clients retry immediately which amplifies the load. logs: 
```
counter 429_count=732 since=2026-03-15T09:12Z
avg_queue_ms=185 p95_queue_ms=860
pool=eu-west-gpu-reserved-4
```
can infra ops add more visibility in responses so SDKs can do wiser pacing? :thinking:

mike: ugh, saw that metric on the dashboard. current admission controller only returns standard `429` with `Retry-After` for hard rejections. we don't surface pool-level load other than opaque rate limits. clients basically get a firehose of 429s and jittered retries.

sre-oncall: repeating what we saw on-call — the retries are causing oscillations. would prefer a signal that suggests "soft backoff" vs "hard rejection" so SDKs can switch to windowed pacing rather than blind exponential backoff.

devx: +1 to richer hints. proposal: add a small set of response headers that are safe to expose and machine-readable. examples: `X-Redwood-Pool-Utilization: 0.86` (0-1), `X-Redwood-Queue-Depth: 12` (requests), and `X-Redwood-Capacity-Hint: 0.3` (fraction of normal throughput allowed). SDKs can use those to scale an internal pacing window.

sam: privacy/security question — can we leak pool utilization? multi-tenant pools might reveal usage patterns. we need to make sure headers are coarse or noisy.

jordan: agree with sam. make it coarse buckets or quantized (e.g., 0-20%,20-40%,... or just low/medium/high). that gives clients enough signal without exposing exact numbers.

mike: good call. implementation idea: admission controller computes a short-lived, per-pool load bucket and emits `X-Redwood-Load: high|med|low` plus `X-Redwood-Queue-Est: <ms>` (rounded). that avoids exact percentages but still actionable.

anya: also: consider including a TTL-limited token `X-Redwood-Admission-Token` for requests that get queued — token can be used by SDKs to re-enqueue without paying full admission cost. helps tail requests avoid redoing cold admission checks. security: signed and short lived.

infra-bot: alert: autoscaler attempted scale-out for eu-west-gpu-reserved-4 at 2026-03-15T09:10Z, result=throttled (quota).

mike: there's also the capacity/finance tradeoff: adding buffer headroom solves the tail but costs $$$. we should measure the cost-per-p99 reduction. rough calc: adding two gpus to pool reduces p99 queue from 860ms -> 320ms but costs ~ $12k/month.

sre-oncall: can we do cheaper mitigations first? e.g., smarter admission (allow small bursts from warm clients), request coalescing for identical prompts, and client pacing hints.

devx: for SDK behavior, suggested semantics (pseudo):
```
if response contains X-Redwood-Load: high -> start pacing window = 50ms + jitter
if X-Redwood-Queue-Est present -> multiply pacing window by (1 + queue_ms/200)
if 429 and no headers -> fallback to full-jitter exp backoff
```
we can expose a public API: RedwoodClient.setPacingHintsEnabled(true) so apps can opt in.

sam: make sure any new headers are opt-in in hosted responses until we validate privacy and perf. also add a flag for Dedicated customers to disable header exposure.

jordan: on token idea — admission tokens should be single-use or limited replays to avoid abuse. include `X-Redwood-Admission-Token-Used: 0/3` so clients know how many requeues left.

mike: operational checklist:
- add coarse load buckets in admission controller (low/med/high) -> infra rollout
- emit rounded queue-est in ms (multiple of 50ms) -> infra rollout
- implement signed admission tokens with 1 minute TTL and max 2 replays -> infra + infra-sec
- expose headers behind a feature flag for hosted; dedicated customers can toggle

anya: testing/metrics to add:
- instrument SDKs to surface when they see Load header so we can correlate client-side pacing -> server-side stability
- add `queue_depth_histogram` per pool and `client_retry_rate` derived metric
- run a canary with a few high-volume customers and measure p95/p99 and token usage

devx: i'll draft SDK changes and a short RFC for header semantics and backoff algo. want to include example flows and a compatibility plan for older SDKs.

sre-oncall: timebox the experiment to 2 weeks. if p99 improves and retries drop without increased errors, we can scale rollout.

anya: action items for today:
- mike + infra to add headers behind a feature flag (eta EOD)
- infra-sec to review token design (eta tomorrow)
- devx to prepare a canary SDK build and doc (eta 48hrs)
- ops to pick 2 eu-west customers for canary (eta 24hrs)

mike: noted. will post PR link when ready.

anya: thanks all — huge win if we can stop the retry storm without buying permanent capacity. :pray:
